subject: Post-call: Token spend runway & batching scenarios — next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Token spend runway & batching scenarios — next steps

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap while items are fresh and to confirm we’re aligned on next steps.

Key pain points you shared:
- Token spend spike on end-of-day batch analytics and personalized history lookups (long contexts).
- Unpredictable per-user cost causing finance gating for the pilot.
- Need to stay within a constrained pilot budget (rough target ~ $12–15k/mo).
- Latency sensitivity for customer-facing flows (95th/99th pct requirements).

Goals you confirmed:
1) Validate a 6-week pilot that demonstrates >=30% reduction in inference unit economics (tokens/unit) while preserving answer quality.
2) Keep 99th pct latency under 350ms for the user-facing endpoint.
3) Produce a TCO view that Finance can sign off on for expansion.

Pilot scope we discussed (proposed):
- Two endpoints: 1) short chat (avg 350 tokens), 2) long-context retrieval (avg 4k tokens).
- Levers to evaluate: batching windows (10–100ms), KV/prefix caching on retrieval paths, and a quantized model variant for cold starts.
- Success metrics: cost per 1k tokens, 95/99 latency, and qualitative score on response accuracy from your sample prompts.

Next steps (from Redwood):
- Share a pilot workbook with scenario-level token economics and three sizing options (conservative / target / aggressive). (attached)
- Schedule a 60-min tech deep-dive this week to validate integration points and KV cache feasibility.
- Provide SOC2 attestation and required audit log fields for procurement review.

Can you confirm the $12k/mo pilot budget constraint (hard or soft)? Also confirm availability for a tech call on Friday morning PT or Monday next week.

Attachments: pilot_scenarios.xlsx (workbook), token-modeling.pdf (TCO summary).

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben on the tech scheduling.

Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Appreciate the clarifications, Alyssa — noted that $12k/mo is the gating constraint. A few concrete datapoints to prep for Friday: 

- Baseline (no batching, no cache, fp16 model): 95th = ~220ms, 99th = ~380ms for the short-chat endpoint; long-context 99th can be 800–1,200ms depending on retrieval pattern.
- Batching (20–50ms window, continuous batching across concurrent requests): short-chat 95/99 improve to ~160ms / ~230ms; long-context 99th often drops by 20–40% depending on average concurrent QPS because KV cache hits short-circuit model runs.
- Prefix/KV caching (50–70% hit rate on historical calls we’ve seen for similar customers): when hit, user-facing latency often falls under 120ms and token cost per call falls drastically (no full forward).
- Quantized variant (8-bit / int8): reduces GPU cost per token by ~15–25% with a small accuracy delta we can measure on your prompt set.

Projected savings (very coarse): combining batching + KV cache we commonly see ~30–55% reduction in token spend for mixed workloads; adding quantization pushes the upper bound toward 60–65% in controlled workloads. Exact outcome depends on your hit rate and concurrency.

Attached is the pilot workbook (pilot_scenarios.xlsx) and a short modeling note (token-modeling.pdf) — those have three sizing options with expected monthly spend and break-even timelines.

Action items: 
- I’ll send an invite for Fri 10:00am PT for the deep-dive.
- Ben, can you bring a short checklist on required log fields and a SOC2 pointer we can share with FinStripe legal?
- Alyssa, if you can confirm contact at Procurement and PO timeline that’ll help us prepare commercial terms.

Thanks,
Dylan

- Retention: configurable per-customer; default 90 days, options to extend for enterprise contracts.
- SOC2 report: https://drive.redwood/soc2/Redwood_SSAE18.pdf (public redacted attestation).
